title: Cross-Domain Solution Control Plane
lede: The control plane API behind a new cross-domain solution running in Azure's air-gapped clouds.

hmDetails.label: problem
hmDetails.body: Air-gapped clouds invalidate most of what a control plane normally leans on. No external dependencies, no shortcuts, and a very high bar for correctness.

hmDetails.label: what i owned
hmDetails.body: Design and development end to end, from resource model through rollout. The service now drives **$4M in monthly recurring revenue**.

engineerDetails.label: constraint
engineerDetails.body: No outbound network. No reachable identity provider, no public package feeds, no telemetry egress, and no hotfix on the normal cadence. Every dependency resolved and vendored before the seal.

engineerDetails.label: approach
engineerDetails.body: Designed the resource model and API surface first, then worked backward to what could actually be satisfied inside the boundary. Deploy and rollback had to be provable offline, so correctness moved left into schema and contract validation.

title: Fleet OS Upgrade Automation
lede: Linux patching across tens of thousands of production servers.

hmDetails.label: problem
hmDetails.body: Every server is somebody's running database. Patching happens monthly and must never become a customer-visible event.

hmDetails.label: what i owned
hmDetails.body: The tooling and the rollout. **40k+ servers monthly** at a sustained **99.98% success rate**.

engineerDetails.label: constraint
engineerDetails.body: Monthly patch cycle across 40k+ Linux VMs, each hosting a live customer database. A reboot is a customer-visible availability event.

engineerDetails.label: approach
engineerDetails.body: Moved upgrade execution into containers so one rollout fans out across the fleet, then split the modes — security-only and allow-listed package sets apply without a reboot. Failure handling is per-node so a bad host doesn't stall the wave.

title: Production Workflow Observability
lede: A secure, read-only window into what production workflows actually did.

hmDetails.label: problem
hmDetails.body: On-call investigations opened with a ~15 minute wait just to see workflow state.

hmDetails.label: what i owned
hmDetails.body: Built it for my team; a sister team adopted it without me driving it. Triage latency dropped to **real time**.

engineerDetails.label: constraint
engineerDetails.body: Engineers needed production workflow state mid-incident, but the data is sensitive and the tool could not become a write path or a new blast radius.

engineerDetails.label: approach
engineerDetails.body: Read-only by construction, scoped access, surfaced live instead of through the batch query path that cost ~15 minutes per lookup.

title: Modern Alchemy Tattoo Co.
lede: Public site, booking platform, and self-service CMS for a tattoo studio in North East, MD.

hmDetails.label: problem
hmDetails.body: The studio's content changes constantly — artists, portfolios, booking availability, announcements. Any design that routed those edits through me would have gone stale within a month.

hmDetails.label: result
hmDetails.body: Owner and artists edit every page, image, and form field themselves through an embedded Sanity Studio and a role-scoped staff portal. **Shipped 2025, still running, zero maintenance requests.**

engineerDetails.label: design
engineerDetails.body: Next.js App Router, server components reading from Sanity. Every page is a CMS document with an `isActive` flag, so the owner can pull a page without a deploy.

engineerDetails.label: auth
engineerDetails.body: NextAuth with Google as sole provider; the session is enriched from the artist record so routes authorize against Owner/Resident/Guest roles rather than a static allowlist.

engineerDetails.label: forms
engineerDetails.body: Booking schemas generated per artist with Zod — available days, budget options, required fields all come from that artist's CMS record. Three booking modes per artist: native form, embedded third-party widget, or external redirect. Images upload straight to Sanity; the admin view subscribes to a Sanity listener so bookings appear without a refresh.
